blocks.text: I can explain how using the same difference rule can make written calculations easier.
In this lesson you will meet Izzy and Sofia. They will show you how to change a subtraction into an easier one with the same answer.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: The minuend is the number being subtracted from.
A subtrahend is a number subtracted from another.
The difference is the result after subtracting one number from another.
A constant is a quantity that has a fixed value that does not change or vary, such as a number.

blocks.text: Izzy writes a sequence of expressions. Each one comes from a ruler showing millimetres.
The minuend and subtrahend are decreasing by 1 mm each time. The difference is constant.
If the minuend and subtrahend are changed by the same amount, the difference remains {constant}.
These expressions all have the same difference. Which would you find easiest to solve mentally?

blocks.label: Tap to see
blocks.text: All three have a difference of 42. The minuend in **70 − 28** is a multiple of 10, which makes it easier to calculate using partitioning.
Izzy’s idea: turn the minuend or the subtrahend into a multiple of 10. Change both numbers by the same amount so the difference stays the same.

rows.note: The subtrahend is now a multiple of 10, so it is easy to do in your head. 53 − 39 = 14 too.

blocks.text: Look for a way to make the minuend or subtrahend a {multiple of 10}.
You can increase or decrease both numbers. Tap each row to build the new calculation.

rows.note: The minuend is now a multiple of 10. 80 − 20 = 60, then 60 − 7 = 53.
The subtrahend is now a multiple of 10.
The minuend is now a multiple of 10. 70 − 40 = 30, then 30 − 5 = 25.

blocks.q: Which change to both numbers makes one of them a multiple of 10? Match each expression to its adjustment.

blocks.text: How could we transform **438 − 389**? Adding 1 to both gives 439 − 390. Sofia says, “I don’t think that has made it easier.”
Izzy sees that 389 is near the next multiple of 100. This is a three-digit number, so using multiples of 100 will be more efficient.

blocks.q: True or false? You can only adjust the subtrahend and minuend by 1 for the difference to remain constant.
blocks.why: You can adjust by any amount, as long as the amount is the same for both numbers. Adjusting by different amounts would change the difference.

blocks.text: Try **35,229 − 15,204**. Subtract 4 from both numbers to create a multiple of 100.
So 35,229 − 15,204 = **20,025**. Partitioning lets us subtract the thousands and hundreds separately.
With **19.67 − 3.95**, a multiple of 100 will not help. These are decimal fractions, so let’s adjust to the nearest one.

rows.note: 3.95 is nearest to the next whole number, 4.
5.03 is close to the whole number 5, so go down.

blocks.text: Izzy uses column subtraction for **30,000 − 3,765**. There is a lot of regrouping (exchanging). Sofia says, “I would use constant difference to transform the calculation first.”

rows.note: The minuend is now full of nines, so there is no regrouping.

blocks.text: It is easier to use a written strategy when no {exchanging} is needed.
Izzy and Sofia both use constant difference on **5.1 − 2.98**, but in different ways.

blocks.label: Same answer?
blocks.text: Yes! Both methods give **2.12**, because the difference stays constant when both numbers change by the same amount.

blocks.q: Pick the new expression that has the same difference AND is easier to solve.

items.q: 72 − 48: make the subtrahend a multiple of 10.
6.96 − 2.03: make the subtrahend a whole number.
517 − 398: which change to both numbers makes 398 a multiple of 100?

blocks.q: Transform the calculation, then choose the answer.

items: If the minuend and subtrahend are changed by the same amount, the difference stays the same or remains constant.
Constant difference is a useful strategy to transform calculations into something more efficient to solve.
By adjusting the minuend and subtrahend carefully, you can make one of them a multiple of 10, 100, 1,000 or one whole, which is easier to calculate with.

blocks.text: Same change to both numbers = same {difference}.

flashcards.front: If the minuend and subtrahend are changed by the same amount, what happens to the difference?
flashcards.back: It stays the same (it remains constant).

flashcards.front: Why do we transform a subtraction using constant difference?
flashcards.back: To make a calculation that is more efficient to solve, for example by making the minuend or subtrahend a multiple of 10.

flashcards.front: Transform 53 − 39 by adding 1 to both numbers. What is the answer?
Transform 68 − 21 by subtracting 1 from both numbers. What is the answer?
Why is 70 − 28 easier to solve mentally than 69 − 27, even though they have the same difference?
flashcards.back:
The minuend is a multiple of 10, so partitioning is easier.

70 − 20 − 8 = 50 − 8 = 42

flashcards.front: True or false? You can only adjust the minuend and subtrahend by 1.
flashcards.back: False. You can adjust by any amount, as long as it is the same amount for both.

flashcards.front: When you transform a three-digit subtraction such as 438 − 389, what should you aim for?
Transform 35,229 − 15,204 by subtracting 4 from both. What is the answer?
When the numbers are decimal fractions, what do we adjust to?
Which tip removes the regrouping from 30,000 − 3,765?
flashcards.back: Subtract 1 from both numbers: 29,999 − 3,764. Then there is no regrouping. The answer is 26,235.

flashcards.front: Complete: it is easier to use a written strategy for subtraction when no ___ is required.
5.1 − 2.98 can be transformed in two ways. What are they?
flashcards.back:
Subtract 0.1 from both: 5.0 − 2.88 = 2.12.
Or add 0.02 to both: 5.12 − 3.00 = 2.12.

questions.prompt: Four of these expressions have the same difference and one does not: 50 − 45, 46 − 41, 52 − 43, 60 − 55, 27 − 22. What is the difference of the odd one out?
questions.explanation: 52 − 43 = 9. The other four all have a difference of 5.

questions.explanation: 97 − 77 = 20. The other four all have a difference of 18.
